title: Structure versus improvisation in early jazz
summary: Early New Orleans bands had wonderful ideas but lacked development; improvising is like a bubble that bursts, while writing records the idea.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: In your great love of structure in music, did you care for the earlier forms of jazz which had seemingly less structure, say the Oliver band, where some of the -- the New Orleans bands. Did you find those not so good, in your eyes?

Well, in a way, I find it this way, that they had wonderful ideas and some of them was lacking of development, real cultivation, development, just the same as if you were to buy a plot of land out there, and tell somebody, I want you to manage that little land out there. I hope I'm making this metaphor clear. They would take that land and they would plant just a few grains here and a grain there, and they wouldn't fully develop your land See?
I see. You can develop things better writing than you can improvising. You can take more time with
Well, I'll go along with you with that, because of this reason. Improvising, you can hit up on some very good things, and sometimes it's like a bubble. It bursts.
You make it, and it's gone, and you say
See, (unintelligible) what the devil is that you made? You say, where, where?

See? You made something that's good. I say, when such and such happened and do so & so, See? Something really good. (unintelligible), you say, oh, I don't know. You say, I don't know, I was just playing.
See? Well, now, thereby, if you were doing the same thing and you were just writing, an idea comes to you and you put that down, that's recorded.

Yeah, I'll go along with writing -- a lot of them say it's mechanical. But I'll go along with it. I'd rather write nine times out of ten, let it be mechanical and now you take it off and play it and play it as though you're thinking. That's what I tell them.
